text:
incident-bot: Pager — high 401 rate on api-prod-eu from multiple edge nodes. 5k req/min, sudden spike at 02:12 UTC. Possible token replay. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/auth-probe

Maya Chen: I'm oncall, looking now. Thanks for the page.

Jo Park: Noted. @Maya can you confirm customer impact? any 5xx or data exfil signs?

Maya Chen: Initial quick check: overall 1.3% of requests returning 401s, two customers (acme-corp, bluebox) seeing elevated error rates and repeated session resets. No 5xx spike. No obvious large downloads in ingress logs yet.

Aaron Li: ACME reported degraded syncs via support ticket #INC-4873. They say retries are looping. I've asked them to share request IDs.

Priya Patel: Copy. Treat as suspicious auth-probe with possible session reuse. Steps: (1) isolate suspicious IPs, (2) enforce short-term session revocation/TTL decrease, (3) scrub logs for PII, (4) rotate any service tokens that might be leaking, (5) notify legal if tokens confirmed leaked.

Ruben Diaz: I'm pulling edge logs now. I see repeated identical Authorization headers across different IPs — looks like proxy replay. Extracting sample and IP list.

Ruben Diaz: Sample IPs to block (temp): 203.0.113.12, 203.0.113.77, 198.51.100.45. Suggest adding deny rule in cloud armor and nginx at edge.

Maya Chen: Agreed. Ruben, please add cloud deny rule and patch edge config. I'll start session TTL tweak and revoke active refresh tokens for affected tenants.

Ruben Diaz: Applied Cloud Armor deny rule: `gcloud compute security-policies rule create --security-policy edge-allow-deny --expression "inIpRange(origin.ip, '203.0.113.0/24')" --action deny --description "temp block suspected replay"`

Ruben Diaz: Also pushed nginx ACL change on edge fleet: `kubectl -n edge patch configmap edge-acl --patch '{"data":{"blocked_ips":"203.0.113.0/24"}}'`

Maya Chen: TTL change: `redis-cli -h auth-cache del tenant:acme:session*` and `POST /admin/sessions/revoke?tenant=acme -H 'Authorization: Bearer <mgmt-token>'` (done for acme + bluebox). Reduced session TTL from 24h -> 5m for affected tenants.

Priya Patel: I'm kicking off a targeted log scrub to remove any potential PII that could be in debug logs forwarded to external buckets. @Ruben add the S3 paths you saw.

Ruben Diaz: Added paths to the scrub job: `s3://edge-logs/prod/2026/03/17/*` and `gs://staging-forwarder/prod-edge/*`. Job queued.

Aaron Li: Support notified ACME and Bluebox with recommended temporary steps (clear local caches, re-auth). ACME says they already rotated their integration key as precaution.

Priya Patel: Next: rotate the service account used by the edge logger-forwarder and suspend its external bucket write while we validate. Aaron, please coordinate with infra to rotate and rekey.

Aaron Li: Infra runbook: creating new key pair and revoking old. Command: `aws iam create-access-key --user-name edge-forwarder` then update pipeline secret and redeploy forwarder. Starting now.

Maya Chen: Monitoring metrics — 401 rate dropped 80% after block + revokes. No new customer-facing data exfil spikes. Marking containment in progress.

Priya Patel: Opening a security incident and pinging Legal. We need to confirm whether tokens were exfiltrated vs replayed. If exfil, we escalate breach process.

Priya Patel: Legal notified: legal@redwood.internal — please standby.

Ruben Diaz: Scrub job returned no files with raw auth headers in external buckets (preliminary). Continue searching internal indexer and any sidecar logs.

Maya Chen: Handing off to next-oncall in 2 hours. Current state: edge deny in place, sessions revoked for affected tenants, forwarder write suspended, rotated forwarder keys (in progress), no confirmed data exfil. Postmortem ticket created: INC-4879.

Jo Park: Thanks team. Can we create a short customer-facing status note for the status page? Quick draft: "We observed repeated unauthorized attempts causing auth failures for a small subset of customers. Mitigation applied; sessions were revoked and suspicious sources blocked. No evidence of customer data exfiltration at this time. We will update as we learn more."

Maya Chen: Fine with that draft. Priya please review before publish.

Priya Patel: Reviewed. Minor wording tweak done. Publish after final infra key rotation confirmation.

Aaron Li: Rotation complete, forwarder redeployed with new keys, old keys revoked at 02:47 UTC.

Maya Chen: Confirmed — traffic normalized. Last check: 401s back to baseline. I'll hand off to @Ruben for follow-up triage and to run the deeper forensic searches. Ruben, please continue and update INC-4879.

Ruben Diaz: Will do. Adding timeline + artifacts to the ticket.

Maya Chen: Handoff: oncall-> @Ruben for follow-up, @Priya for security investigation, @Jo for customer comms. Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring.

incident-bot: Incident assigned -> INC-4879 (security:investigate).

Maya Chen: Thanks all, closing active paging. Follow-up meeting scheduled 03/17 10:00 UTC.
